title: Co-fractionation/mass spectrometry to identify protein complexes
protocol: Wash any preservatives or wetting agents from a 3k MWCO AcroPrep Advance 96 filter plate by adding a 300-μL volume of LC/MS-grade H2O and pulling it through the membrane using vacuum.
Condition the filter plate by adding a 300-μL volume of Trypsin Digestion Buffer and pulling the solution through the membrane using vacuum.
Do not let the wells dry out during washes to prevent proteins from sticking irreversibly to the membrane.
Shake excess liquid from the washed plate after stopping the vacuum.
Transfer samples to the washed AcroPrep plate.
Apply vacuum to reduce sample volume to approximately 100 μL.
Add Trypsin Digestion Buffer to each well until the total volume is 100 μL.
Mix using several aspirate and dispense cycles with a pipette.
Continue vacuum filtration to reduce the sample volume to approximately 50 μL.
Transfer concentrated samples back into the original deep well plate for digestion.
Add 50 μL of 100% TFE to each sample.
Add sufficient volume of 0.5 M TCEP stock for a final concentration of 5 mM in each sample well.
Seal the plate with clear film and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Place the plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add sufficient volume of 550 mM iodoacetamide stock for a final concentration of 15 mM in each sample well.
Seal the plate and incubate for 30 minutes in the dark, at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Thaw iodoacetamide stock solution directly prior to use.
Quench unreacted iodoacetamide by adding sufficient volume of the 1 M DTT stock for a final concentration of 7.5 mM in each sample well.
Add ~880-μL volume of Trypsin Digestion Buffer to bring each sample to a final volume of 1 mL.
Add 10 μL volume (1 μg of enzyme) of proteomics-grade Trypsin stock solution in 10 mM acetic acid to each well.
Seal the plate with clear film and digest overnight at 37°C.
Stop protein digestion by adding sufficient volume of formic acid for a final concentration of 0.1% (v/v) per sample well.
Condition each utilized well of the C18 Lab-in-a-Plate using vacuum filtration as follows: Add 100 μL volume of the 60% Buffer B per well and vacuum through.
Repeat conditioning with a second addition of 100 μL volume of the 60% Buffer B per well.
Add a 100 μL volume of Buffer A per well and vacuum filter through.
Repeat the previous step 3–4 times.
Add a 1 mL volume of each sample to an individual conditioned well on the plate, and apply vacuum to filter the samples through.
Wash the wells by adding a 100 μL volume of Buffer A, and apply vacuum to filter.
Repeat the washing step 2 more times.
Elution at <−15 Hg is recommended; place a 96-well collection plate into the appropriate vacuum manifold adaptor to collect the eluate.
Elute the digested peptides into the collection plate using a 50 μL volume of 60% Buffer B per well.
Repeat the elution step a second time for a total eluate volume of 100 μL.
Evaporate the eluate solvent in a vacuum centrifuge to dryness.
Resuspend peptides in a 20- to 35-μL volume of Buffer C per well.
Pipette up and down several times to mix thoroughly.
Transfer the reconstituted sample to the appropriate sample vial or plate for your autosampler system.
Store unused sample at −80°C in sealed plates for long-term storage.
Prepare protein fractions for MS analysis using Method 2 if the sample contains < 300 mM salt.
Ensure that the bottom of wells can make good contact with the magnetic slab.
Have aliquots of beads prepared as described below.
Reconstitute hydrophilic beads provided as a 50 mg/mL slurry with preservative.
Vortex-mix and pipette thoroughly to ensure homogeneity.
Reconstitute hydrophobic beads provided as a 50 mg/mL slurry with preservative.
Vortex-mix and pipette thoroughly to ensure homogeneity.
Combine 50 μL of each bead suspension in a single microcentrifuge tube.
Mix well by vortexing or pipetting.
Collect the beads by low-speed pulse centrifugation.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Wash the beads by thorough resuspension in 1 mL LC/MS-grade H2O.
Repeat steps to collect and wash the beads.
Resuspend beads in a 500-μL volume of LC/MS-grade H2O for a working microparticle dispersion density of 10 μg/μL total.
Aliquot the slurry for ease of resuspension.
Store aliquots at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Thoroughly resuspend beads before each use.
Add TFE to sample wells to achieve a final concentration of 20% TFE.
Mix by pipetting.
Add TCEP stock to achieve a final concentration of 5 mM in each sample well.
Seal the plate with adhesive film.
Incubate the plate for 45 minutes at 37°C.
Place the plate at room temperature after incubation.
Add iodoacetamide stock to achieve a final concentration of 25 mM in each sample well.
Incubate for 30 min in the dark at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Quench reactivity by adding sufficient volume of 1 M DTT stock to achieve a final concentration of 12 mM in each sample well.
To each fraction, add a 4-μL volume of bead suspension, which is a 1:1 mix of two bead types at 5 μg/mL each.
Add a sufficient volume of formic acid for a final concentration of 2% (v/v).
Add a sufficient volume of acetonitrile for a final solvent proportion of 50% (v/v) and mix well by pipetting.
Mix gently but thoroughly by pipetting.
Incubate for 30 min with gentle shaking or rocking to keep beads from settling.
Centrifuge briefly (e.g., 5 min at 1,000 × g) in a swinging bucket rotor equipped with deep well plate adaptors to collect beads.
Place the sample plate on the magnetic plate and remove bulk liquid, leaving behind the beads and approximately 250 μL of liquid.
Resuspend the beads in the remaining liquid and transfer them to a fresh conical bottom 450 μL 96-well plate.
Place the shallow plate on the magnetic plate.
Remove and discard the remaining liquid once beads have collected at the bottom.
Wash with a 100 μL volume of 70% ethanol per well.
Repeat the ethanol wash step a second time.
Wash with a 100 μL volume of acetonitrile per well.
Repeat the acetonitrile wash step a second time.
Air dry the beads briefly.
Resuspend the beads in a 25-μL volume of 10% TFE prepared in Trypsin Digestion Buffer solution.
Dilute trypsin stock solution with trypsin digestion buffer for the next step.
Add a 25 μL volume of Trypsin Digestion Buffer containing 0.25 μg of proteomics-grade Trypsin to each sample.
Seal the plate with adhesive film.
Incubate overnight (12–16 h) at 37°C.
Place the sample plate on the magnet once more.
Transfer the bead-free supernatant to a fresh 96-well plate after beads have collected.
Add a sufficient volume of formic acid to achieve a final concentration of 1% (v/v) to stop protein digestion.
Remove the plate from the 96-well magnetic plate separator.
Elute peptides from the beads with a 50-μL volume of a 2% DMSO solution.
Cover samples with adhesive film and sonicate for 5 minutes in a bath sonicator to assist elution (optional).
Replace the plate on the 96-well magnetic plate separator to collect the beads.
Remove each sample eluate and add it to the corresponding supernatant from step 14a.
Remove the plate from the magnet again.
Elute the beads with another 50-μL volume of a 2% DMSO solution without sonication.
Replace this bead plate on the magnetic plate separator.
Remove this second volume of eluate and pool it with the first corresponding matched eluate for a total volume of 150 μL for each fraction.
Desalt the eluted peptides using the conditioned solid-phase C18 Lab-in-a-Plate, loading 150 μL instead of 1 mL as in Method 1.
